newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia grain consumption seen outpacing production.
newsitem.headline: Asia grain consumption seen outpacing production.

text.p: Asian consumption of wheat, coarse grains and rice will probably outpace production in the region, the executive director of the International Grains Council (IGC) said on Thursday.

IGC executive director Richard Woodhams said in a paper on the first day of the Asia rice conference in Singapore that if dietary patterns in the region remained unchanged, Asia would "consume approximately 32 million tonnes more wheat, 48 million tonnes more rice and 31 million tonnes more feed grains than it did in 1996."
"Meeting the region's food and feed needs will therefore require more grain imports, mostly from outside the region," he said.
The rapidly developing economies in Asia will also spur a rapid expansion of meat consumption.

"Higher GNPs (gross national product) will bring many more people into the income ranges where meat consumption becomes possible," Woodhams said. "Grain demand for feed seems likely to continue to grow rapidly over the next few years."
Even a moderate increase in world grain prices over the next decade will have little impact on the growth of grain imports into the region, he added.
